holidays.name: National Cherry Popsicle Day
holidays.description: A day for cooling off with a icy, bright-red cherry popsicle at the tail end of summer. Lick fast, because August heat doesn't wait. Cherry is one of the most beloved popsicle flavors, so this is an easy holiday to celebrate.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture of the late-summer food-holiday calendar.
holidays.funFact: Cherry is often called the most popular popsicle flavor in the U.S. Many 'cherry' treats get their flavor from a blend that has little to do with real cherries.

holidays.name: National Toilet Paper Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the humble roll we only appreciate when it runs out. Celebrate by restocking your supply, and take a moment to be grateful for modern comfort.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors a household staple that most people take for granted.
holidays.funFact: Packaged toilet paper was first sold in the United States in 1857 by Joseph Gayetty. It was medicated paper sold in flat sheets, not rolls.

holidays.name: National Dog Day
holidays.description: A day to shower your four-legged best friend with belly rubs, walks, and treats. It also highlights the need to adopt and rescue dogs of every breed and mix.
holidays.origin: Pet and family lifestyle expert and animal advocate Colleen Paige founded it in 2004. She picked August 26 because it was the day her family adopted her childhood dog, Sheltie, when she was ten.
holidays.funFact: Roughly 3 million dogs enter U.S. shelters each year, and the day is one of the biggest pet-themed hashtag days of the year.
